verdicts.evidence: `if (!id)` forced false lets an absent id fall through to the table lookups, which answer null for it anyway: GATE_HOOK_HARNESSES.includes(undefined) is false and familyOfHarness(undefined) matches no signal. Measured: resolveGateHookHarness over undefined, null, "", claude, claude-code, gemini-cli, cursor, codex and an unknown id returns the same value on both builds (0 of 4,545 direct cases differ), and the 121 command runs are byte-identical. Survived the CI unit pass on this branch and the whole-net pass of 2026-09-29 (scripts/mutation-wholenet.mjs, seven legs, serial). Measurement: identical on all 11 missions × 11 commands (121 runs); 0 of 4545 direct calls differ. Probe suite 2026-09-28 (scratch recipe, reproduced in the PR): eleven missions built with the pristine 0.42.3-dev build — `init` (blank), `init --example`, and the example with a dead pointer, the regulated tier on, a drifted seal, an edited and a removed rule, a failing after-hook, no scaffold-lock (unrecorded corpus), an under-filled framing note, a DRAFT ADR, and a fresh mission with two agent ratifications. Each mutant was spliced alone into dist/lib and eleven commands were run on each mission (check with and without --strict, --json, --sarif, --hooks; gate-hook for claude, cursor and gemini), exit code, stdout and stderr compared byte for byte with the pristine build. Positive control: the killed mutants gate-hook L77 and sarif L161 applied the same way differ on the regulated mission.
